text:
Anya: quick note — trying to bring up llama-2-13b q4f16 (HF weights) across AWS/GCP/Azure A100v4 (same SKU) and seeing different p99 tails even when driver+CUDA look identical. anyone seen this?

Miguel: what driver/CUDA are you pinning?

Anya: pinning NVIDIA driver 535.86 and CUDA 12.2. images are ubuntu-22.04. job: single-replica inference, seq=1024, batch=1, gen tokens=512. runtime: our engine with fused-attn + cutlass kernels.

Sean: interesting — did you check MIG/SM versioning and BIOS power settings? cloud images sometimes ship different microcode.

Anya: yes — MIG not enabled, SM reported 8.0. did an initial check on BIOS/power; looked same. perf-bot posted a run with histograms + kernel traces: https://perf.example.com/runs/1805123456

perf-bot: auto-benchmark summary
- AWS (us-west-2, A100-80GB): p50=45ms p95=78ms p99=142ms throughput=210 tok/s
- GCP (us-west1, A100-80GB): p50=42ms p95=66ms p99=98ms throughput=230 tok/s
- Azure (westeurope, A100-80GB): p50=48ms p95=95ms p99=210ms throughput=190 tok/s

Lisa: whoa, Azure tail is bad. kernel traces show frequent fallback to generic attention kernel at long sequences.

Anya: exact — trace snippet shows mix of cutlass/fused_attn then spikes of "attn_trust_fallback".

Sean: can you paste the kernel list from nvprof/nvtx? also check cuBLAS version; some cutlass paths require >= cuBLAS 12.1.

Anya: clipped logs:
```
KERNEL: fused_attn_forward (cutlass-sm80)  21.3ms
KERNEL: kv_cache_update  3.5ms
KERNEL: attn_trust_fallback  110.2ms
KERNEL: cudnn_convolution  2.1ms
```

Miguel: did you build the runtime with the same compiler flags across clouds? saw ABI diffs when gcc 11 vs 12 changed kernel behavior.

Anya: builds from same docker image SHA but host glibc and packaging differ by patchlevel. suspect host driver packaging influences kernel selection.

Evan: also check PFN mapping — GPUDirect/IOMMU differences can cause page-fault retries and long tails.

Lisa: let's reproduce with a minimal microbench that exercises long-attn hot path and captures per-kernel latencies.

Sean: +1. Script to run:
```
./scripts/attn_microbench.sh --seq 1024 --batch 1 --iters 200 --cuda 12.2 --capture-kernels
```

Anya: running that across the three clouds now. uploading logs to run dir.

perf-bot: upload links:
- AWS: https://s3.amazonaws.com/redwood-perf/1805123456/aws.log
- GCP: https://storage.googleapis.com/redwood-perf/1805123456/gcp.log
- AZR: https://mystorage.azure/redwood-perf/1805123456/azr.log

Miguel: quick diff of kernel histograms GCP vs AZR: AZR shows ~6x more fallback-attn invocations and ~2x more small page-fault retries.

Anya: note: disabling cudagraphs on Azure reduced p99 from 210ms -> 120ms but throughput dropped ~8%. implies interaction between cudagraphs and kernel selection/JIT.

Evan: that smells like driver-level launch batching / cudart behavior affecting JIT or kernel cache. which libcudart/libcudnn are you linking? system or statically bundled?

Anya: we use system libcudart from the driver package; libcudnn is also system-installed.

Lisa: hypothesis test: force cutlass-only path with REDWOOD_FORCE_CUTLASS=1 and re-run to see if azure still falls back.

Anya: forced-cutlass run on Azure: p99 -> 130ms, better but still worse than GCP 98ms. fused_attn timings present but variance high.

Sean: check GPU clocks and power policy during runs. Azure hosts sometimes have adaptive governors that oscillate clocks.

Anya: polled clocks via nvidia-smi: AWS/GCP steady at 1140 MHz; AZR oscillated between 720 -> 1410 MHz over the run. looks like governor oscillation correlates with tail spikes.

Miguel: that explains a lot. toggling clocks mid-run can cause kernel slowdowns and context-related stalls.

Evan: mitigation options we tested:
- set persistent performance mode via nvidia-smi (-pm 1) and lock clocks (-lgc 1410,1410) if host allows
- add runtime warmup to prime freq governors before serving
- prefer Dedicated instances with known host configs

Anya: added a warmup loop and set NVML policy to max perf with nvidia-smi -pm 1; nvidia-smi -lgc 1410,1410 on Azure. p99 improved to ~102ms (near GCP).

Lisa: great. let's document this in the model bring-up checklist for cross-cloud testing:
- verify driver version + libcudart/cudnn packaging (system vs container)
- check host perf governor & GPU clocks during bench runs
- run attn_microbench with --capture-kernels and collect histograms
- diff kernel lists for fallback patterns and page-faults
- test cudagraphs on vs off and measure tail impact
- force kernel paths (cutlass vs fallback) to isolate JIT/runtime causes
- record CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES & PCIe topology mapping

Miguel: add note about compiler/ABI consistency (gcc toolchain) and host libc patchlevels. also record PCIe peer-to-peer topology; device 0 mapping differed on one Azure SKU and caused small memcpy stalls.

Anya: will put final notes + scripts into the perf run dir and open a small PR to add to the onboarding doc. thanks all :tada:

perf-bot: thread marked resolved by Anya at 1805123499

Anya: closing — next step: formalize infra guardrails for Dedicated pool images (pin perf governor, bundle driver libs).
